newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Germany's Kohl looks forward to working with Blair.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl looks forward to working with Blair.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday the Labour Party's overwhelming victory in the British general election showed Britons did not like anti-European polemics.
Kohl, speaking in Brunei during an Asian tour, said he hoped Labour leader Tony Blair would support the European Union more than the outgoing Conservative government had.
Offering his cooperation with the new prime minister, Kohl said he would meet Blair the week after next and expected to get to know him better at a special EU summit later this month.

"This is an overwhelming mandate for the new government," said Kohl, whose strongly pro-European policies irritated Conservative "Eurosceptics". One Conservative campaign poster portrayed him as a pro-EU ventriloquist with Blair as a dummy on his knee.

"Voters did not like the anti-European rhetoric of the past few days and weeks and this should be a lesson for all those who want to win votes with anti-European polemics," Kohl told reporters travelling with him. He later left for Australia.
Asked about Blair's stand on the EU's planned economic and monetary union (EMU), Kohl said he had read the Labour policy platform very carefully and found it cautious on this point.
"I would welcome it if Labour were more friendly towards Europe than the Conservatives were," he said.
Kohl, who liked to call outgoing Prime Minister John Major "my friend John", said he would do all he could to support policies that kept Britain involved in Europe.
The chancellor announced last month he would run for a record fifth term next year, mostly because he wanted to stay on to see Europe's single currency launched in 1999.

One potential Social Democrat (SPD) challenger, Gerhard Schroeder, has been toying with a mildly anti-European campaign to exploit German voters' distaste at the idea of giving up the strong mark for the euro currency.
